articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Pulsed Power Applications' (Digest No.135)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: Railguns can easily exceed the muzzle velocity limit of conventional guns, however this requires the use of driving currents of over 1 million amperes. In the simplest railgun barrel configuration, the driving current flows in a loop formed by the projectile armature, the conducting rails and the power supply. The author looks at the plasma armature, the simplest type of armature to use, requiring only the generation of a plasma behind the projectile.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of pulsed power to KrF lasers and the application of KrF lasers to pulsed power
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: The author considers the requirements of pulsed power for high power, electron-beam-excited KrF lasers. He then looks at the topic of laser-triggered switching, where small discharge-excited KrF lasers have been used to great effect in high-voltage gas switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: For some military applications such as anti-armour and air defence, increasing muzzle velocity leads to significant increases in weapon performance. The EM railgun has already demonstrated velocities in excess of 10 km/sec and muzzle energies over 6 MJ, and ideally requires a high current, low voltage pulsed power system. The author describes options and problems associated with railguns and their power supplies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: Because of space charge limitations high energy particle beam facilities comprise a series of coupled machines where particles are successively accelerated to higher energies. Kicker magnets are the fast beam switching devices which permit high efficiency transfer of these particle beams from one circular accelerator to the next. The author describes the switching processes of kicker magnets. The pulse durations for kicker excitations do not exceed the beam circulation time in the synchrotron which is in the range 600-2100 ns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: The author determines the feasibility of linear induction accelerators as tubular travelling wave machines for use as projectile accelerators. A model of the accelerator is presented and performance characteristics, rotor heating and a sample outline design are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Current trends in pulsed power radar technology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: Radar power supplies continue to be a major area of application for modern power electronics. Several factors have had a major influence on the design of pulsed power supplies for radar systems. These are: digital signal processing; fast switching power semiconductors; and development of components. Typical modern radar transmitters are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: All-solid-state pulsers for gas laser excitation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: From the point of view of reliability and long operating life, it is desirable for as much of the electrical system of a pulsed gas laser to make use of solid state devices. Until new solid state laser development catches up with performance levels of current repetitively pulsed excimer, TEA CO/sub 2/ and copper vapour lasers, it has to be accepted that a major component of the total system is basically gaseous electronics. However there is considerable scope to ensure that the rest of the system is of the reliable solid state variety. The use of thyristors as the primary switch, coupled to magnetic pulse compression is discussed in terms of the possible circuit formats and the capabilities of both thyristors and magnetic materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Plasma heating systems on the JET Tokamak
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: JET is the largest project in the Euratom fusion research programme. Its objective is to obtain and study plasmas with parameters and dimensions approaching those needed in a fusion reactor. However, to obtain the temperatures required for a reactor heating by a current is insufficient and so JET is equipped with two additional forms of heating, namely neutral beam heating and radio frequency heating. The author describes these two forms of heating.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermonuclear fusion magnet pulsed power systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: Research into the confinement of high temperature plasmas by magnetic fields with the ultimate aim of generating thermonuclear fusion power has been in progress for the last 30 years. The two best magnetic field configurations at present are the Tokamak and reversed field pinch. These magnetic fusion machines require pulsed power systems and switching systems which are both described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hydrogen thyratrons and their applications-an overview
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: A hydrogen thyratron is a high voltage, high peak current, repetitive switch. When triggered with a positive pulse of a few hundred volts, it will switch thousands of amps very accurately in absolute time at high repetition rates. The author describes the development of hydrogen thyratrons and various applications including particle accelerators, linear accelerators and pulsed lasers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The hydrogen thyratron in radar today
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: In radar the transmitted pulse is defined in duration, peak power and timing by a modulator. The hydrogen thyratron soon superseded all other switching devices on its introduction as it could reduce drift and jitter. The uses of thyratrons in radar for pulse modulation and crowbar applications are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pulsed power techniques for discharge pumped visible and ultraviolet excimer lasers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: Excimer lasers of the rare-gas halide type can be pumped by pulsed electron beams, optically via an appropriate photo-dissociation step, and by pre-ionised high pressure glow discharge. The author describes the design requirements of the pulsed power supplies that are needed for high pressure glow discharge pumping and how these requirements have been met in the design of a number of discharge pumped excimer lasers that have recently been built at St. Andrews University.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of pulsed power to inertial confinement fusion
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Pulsed Power Applications
abstract: The inertial confinement approach to fusion has the advantage over magnetic containment in that the technique has been verified on a large scale with thermonuclear weapons. The challenge is to make it happen on the laboratory scale with the nuclear driver replaced by a more conventional source of pulsed power. In order to compress a sufficient mass of D-T fuel to 1000* liquid density and heat it to the 10/sup 8/ degrees required for ignition, power has to be supplied to a few mm dia. fuel pellet at a rate of up to 10/sup 15/ W for a duration of 10 ns or so (i.e. a pulse energy of up to 10 MJ). This power can be delivered to the pellet either by photons (laser fusion) or by ions (ion-beam fusion). Both approaches involve the application of pulsed power in very large proportions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
